description_en: This two-storey pagoda-style Triliṅgeśvara temple in Bāhālukhāṭolastands on a single plinth and faces west. The sanctum houses aśivaliṅgaknown as Sadāśiva. It features a squareyoniwith threeliṅgain it. The sanctum's floor is paved in stone and three of its walls are lined with oil lamp balustrades. Atoraṇawith images of Umā and Maheśvara is fixed above the entrance. Alongside its intricate carvings, the door of the temple is flanked by miniature aedicules with carvings of celestial spirits. Further aedicules can be found to the north, south and east, each with an opening to allow spirits to travel through unhindered (dyaḥpvaḥ).  A five-layerd timber cornice, which is standard for most temples of the Malla period, seperates the ground floor from the upper portion. Carved timber windows on all sides are flanked by carved panels. Both the temple's roofs are supported by 12 struts, and the pinnacle is made from gilt copper. The second tier struts are carved in the Sālabhañjikā style.A small stonenandīis installed in typical fahion to the west of the temple. Further west, a brick-paved square measuring 90 x 90 cm is used for the sacred fire (hom). A Bhairava shrine with three cusped archedṭoraṇaon a stone platform is located next to the temple's southern plinth. Local people conductDigupūjāat this shrine. According to the priest, the large stone platform to the south of the temple, was the sacred place where rituals for the temple's consecration were held. Previously, stepping on the platform was considered inauspicious.  A Bhairavī shrine is located on the south side of the courtyard, next to the road. The north eastern corner is home to a Viṣṇu shrine and a temple to Gaṇeśa (LAL02510) can be found in the north-western corner of the courtyard. There are also twophalcāsin the temple complex.A Licchavi inscription which dates back toSamvat435 and makes reference to King Vasantadeva (r. 506-532) is attached to the western plinth of the temple (VajracharyaVS 2030: 112).Kīrtipatākā,a poem composed by Kunu Śarmā in 1652, mentions Bāhālukhāṭolaand this temple in its 22nd verse.Svasthānīvratakathā, a text composed in the Valley around the 18th century, mentions the 51 shrines of Lord Śiva and also refers to the Triliṅgeśvara Mandira. It is possible that the shrine mentioned is this very temple. The temple is referred to as Trinetra Mahādeva.Pruscha(1975: 137) dates this temple to the 16th century.In 1994 CE, the temple was restored through the combined effort of local stakeholders and the Urban Development through Locat Efforts Project (UDLE).The grounds of the temple complex used to be paved with brick. In 2022, the Lalitpur Municipality replaced the brick with stone paving. Today, the entire square is used as a parking lot.
description_ne: इखालखु र पूर्णचण्डी टोलको बीच भागमा अवस्थित बाहालुखा टोलमा यो मन्दिर रहेको छ ।  कुनु शर्माले कीर्तिपटाकामा यस टोलको वर्णन गर्दै राम्रा झ्याल र ढोकाले कुबेरको अलका झैं सुशोभित भनेका छन् भने त्रिलेङ्गेश्वरलाई त्रिनेत्र नामक महादेव भनेका छन् (Narahari Nātha, 2018 VS, 7 रPruscha1975, 137)  ले यस मन्दिरको निर्माणकाल १६ औं शताब्दी भनेका छन् । एक तहको पेटीमाथि दुई तले पेगोडा शैलीमा निर्मित यो मन्दिर पश्चिमाभिमुख छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा चतुष्कोणाकार शिवलिङ्ग रहेको छ जुन त्रिलिङ्गेश्वरको साथै सदाशिवको नामले चिनिन्छ । गर्भगृहमा मुल शिललिङ्ग बाहेक अन्य दुई साना शिवलिङ्गहरू छन् । यसरी यहाँ शिवलिङ्गको कुल संख्या तीन भएकोले त्रिलिङ्गेश्वर भनिएको भनाई स्थानीयको रहेको छ ।  शिवलिङ्गतिर फर्काइएको साढेको मूर्ति मन्दिरको पश्चिममा स्थापित छ ।  मन्दिरमा एउटै मात्र प्रवेशद्वार छ र द्वारको माथि कलात्मक तोरण रहेको छ । तोरणको सबैभन्दा उचो भागमा उमामहेश्वर कुँदिएको छ भने मध्य भागमा गरूड र तल्लो भागम तीनवटा उभिएका मूर्तिहरू कुँदिएका छन् । मन्दिरको पहिलो र दोस्रो तल्लको छानो समान १२\१२ वटा टुंडालहरूले थामेको छ । पहिलो तल्लाका टुंडालहरूको बीच भागमा विभिन्न भैरवका मूर्तिहरू कुँदिएका छन् भने दोस्रो तल्लाकोमा सालभञ्जिका देख्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तामाको गजूर रहेको छ ।मन्दिर परिसरमा अन्य पीठहरूका साथै एउटा इनार पनि रहेको छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिणी पेटीसंगै भैरवको पीठ टाँसिएर रहेको छ । मन्दिरबाटै दक्षिणमा दशमहाविद्या अन्तर्गतको भैरवी पीठ रहेको छ । मन्दिरको ईशान कोणमा सानो विष्णुमूर्ति सहितको shrine छ भने वायव्य कोणमा गणेशको मन्दिर छ । मन्दिर नजिकै उत्तरमा फल्चा छ भने मन्दिर  भन्दा अलिक पर आग्नेय कोणमा पनि एक फल्चा रहेको छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिणमा गिरी खलक वस्दै आएको मठ रहेको छ । मन्दिरको पश्चिमी पेटीसंगै लिच्छवि राजा वसन्तदेवको संवत् ४३५को अभिलेख टाँसिएर रहेको छ(VajrācāryaVS 2056: 272) ।स्वस्थानी व्रत कथामा उल्लेखित ५१ शिव पीठहरूमा त्रिलिङ्गेश्वर नाम पनि उल्लेखित छ । नजिकैको मठमा वस्दै आएका गिरी खलकको निजी गुठी अन्तर्गत मन्दिरमा नित्य पूजा लगायत अन्य धार्मिक गतिविधि संचालन हुँदै आएको छ ।

references: Sources and references Inscription identification number LAL0250_I_001 Sources This stone inscription by King Vasanta Deva (r. 506-532) stands against the plinth on the northwest corner of the temple. It was first published in the "Abhilekha Saṃgraha, part- 5 by Itihāsa Saṃśodhana Maṇḍala. It was also published by Vajracharya (VS 2030,112). According to Dhanavajra Vajracharya, the upper part of the inscription was found damaged and the lower half was buried. size of stone stele: H: 56 cm, W: 60 cm size of inscrition fragment on the left: H: 12 cm, W: 10 cm

historical_events.event_description: This stone inscription by King Vasanta Deva (r. 506-532) stands against the plinth on the northwest corner of the temple.In the 1970s when Dhanavajra Vajracharya documented the inscription (Vajracharya(VS 2030,112), he found the upper part severely damaged with most of the letters rubbed off and the lower section buried.
Offering of thetoraṇawhich is installed above the main entrance to the temple.
Amara Girī Gusāyī established aguṭhīfor the daily and casual worship at the temple.
Jitgovinda Amātya and his family supported the renovation of the temple.
Endowment of areas of land to the trust of the deity. This document appoints Lakṣmī Girī Gosāi as priest and allows him to use the trust.

Thislālamoharaof King Gīrvāṇa appoints Lakṣmī Girī Gosāī̃ as the priest to conduct the routine rituals of Śrī Triliṅgeśvara Mahādeva of Bahālukhā Ikhālakhu, Patan, using produce from the bestowed land in value of 10 ropanīs.
In 1994 CE, the temple was restored through the combined effort of local stakeholders and the Urban Development through Locat Efforts (UDLE) project .

historical_events.event_description: The Lalitpur Municipality paved the courtyard with flagstone laid in cement mortar.
